title: "zoneinfo" should be preferred to "pytz" when using Python 3.9 and later
description: The `pytz` library has been the de facto standard for timezone handling in Python for many years. However, Python 3.9 introduced the `zoneinfo` module as part of the standard library, providing a modern, standardized approach to timezone handling. The `zoneinfo` module is now the recommended way to work with timezones and should be preferred over `pytz` for new code when using Python 3.9 or later versions.
message: Replace usage of 'pytz' with the standard library 'zoneinfo' module for Python 3.9+.
impact: Using `pytz` instead of the standard library `zoneinfo` module adds an unnecessary external dependency, increases the attack surface, and may lead to compatibility issues in the future. The `zoneinfo` module provides better performance, follows modern Python standards, and is actively maintained as part of the Python standard library.
recommendation: Replace imports and usage of `pytz` with the `zoneinfo` module. Update timezone creation from `pytz.timezone()` to `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo()`, and use `datetime.now(tz=ZoneInfo('timezone'))` instead of `datetime.now(pytz.timezone('timezone'))`.

references.title: PEP 615 - Support for the IANA Time Zone Database in the Standard Library
Real Python - Working With Python Datetime and Timezones

noncompliant.code:
import pytz
from datetime import datetime

# Using pytz for timezone creation
eastern = pytz.timezone('US/Eastern')
now = datetime.now(eastern)

# Using pytz.utc
utc_time = datetime.now(pytz.utc)

# Localizing with pytz
naive_dt = datetime(2023, 10, 15, 12, 0)
localized_dt = eastern.localize(naive_dt)
noncompliant.description: Using pytz for timezone handling when Python 3.9+ standard library zoneinfo is available.

compliant.code:
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# Using zoneinfo for timezone creation
eastern = ZoneInfo('US/Eastern')
now = datetime.now(eastern)

# Using standard library UTC
utc_time = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

# Creating timezone-aware datetime directly
aware_dt = datetime(2023, 10, 15, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo('US/Eastern'))
compliant.description: Using the standard library zoneinfo module for timezone handling, which is the recommended approach for Python 3.9+.

why_is_this_an_issue: The `pytz` library, while historically important, is now superseded by the standard library `zoneinfo` module in Python 3.9+. Continuing to use `pytz` introduces unnecessary external dependencies, increases the project's attack surface, and may lead to maintenance challenges. The `zoneinfo` module provides equivalent functionality with better integration into the Python ecosystem, improved performance, and guaranteed long-term support as part of the standard library.
how_to_fix: Replace `pytz` imports and usage with the `zoneinfo` module: 1. Change `import pytz` to `from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo`. 2. Replace `pytz.timezone('timezone_name')` with `ZoneInfo('timezone_name')`. 3. Replace `pytz.utc` with `datetime.timezone.utc`. 4. Update timezone-aware datetime creation to use `datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second, tzinfo=ZoneInfo('timezone'))`. 5. Remove the pytz dependency from your requirements file after ensuring all usage has been migrated.
